from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Superposition is a linear combination of base states.",
            "The formula is |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩.",
            "α and β are called probability amplitudes.",
            "Their squared values must always sum to one.",
            "This allows particles to exist in multiple places."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining Superposition: The Linear Combination", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Superposition is a linear combination of base states.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        
        formula = MathTex(
            r"|\psi\rangle", "=", r"\alpha", "|0\rangle", "+", r"\beta", "|1\rangle",
            color="#ADD8E6",
            font_size=42
        )
        # B002: horizontally extended mobjects use place_in_area spanning multiple columns
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A2', 'A5')
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The formula is |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # α and β are called probability amplitudes.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # Highlight alpha and beta
        alpha_rect = SurroundingRectangle(formula[2], color="#FFFF00", buff=0.1)
        beta_rect = SurroundingRectangle(formula[5], color="#FFFF00", buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(alpha_rect), Create(beta_rect))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Their squared values must always sum to one.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        sum_formula = MathTex(r"|\alpha|^2 + |\beta|^2 = 1", color=WHITE, font_size=36)
        # Place below the main formula
        self.place_in_area(sum_formula, 'B3', 'B4')
        
        self.play(Write(sum_formula))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This allows particles to exist in multiple places.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Rooms
        room_left = Rectangle(width=2.0, height=1.5, color=WHITE)
        room_right = Rectangle(width=2.0, height=1.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # B040: position symmetrically relative to the vertical center line
        self.place_in_area(room_left, 'C1', 'E3')
        self.place_in_area(room_right, 'C4', 'E6')
        
        label_left = Text("Left Room", font_size=20)
        label_right = Text("Right Room", font_size=20)
        
        # B001: Labels outside the room areas
        self.place_at_grid(label_left, 'F2')
        self.place_at_grid(label_right, 'F5')
        
        self.play(
            Create(room_left), Create(room_right),
            Write(label_left), Write(label_right)
        )
        
        # Quarky Ghost helper function
        def get_quarky(color=WHITE, opacity=1.0):
            body = Circle(radius=0.4, color=color, fill_opacity=opacity, stroke_opacity=opacity)
            eye_l = Dot(radius=0.06, color=BLACK).move_to(body.get_center() + 0.15*UP + 0.15*LEFT)
            eye_r = Dot(radius=0.06, color=BLACK).move_to(body.get_center() + 0.15*UP + 0.15*RIGHT)
            return VGroup(body, eye_l, eye_r)

        # Initial ghost state: alpha=0.7, beta=0.7
        quarky_left = get_quarky(color=BLUE, opacity=0.7)
        quarky_right = get_quarky(color=RED, opacity=0.7)
        
        self.place_in_area(quarky_left, 'C1', 'E3')
        self.place_in_area(quarky_right, 'C4', 'E6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(quarky_left), FadeIn(quarky_right))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Adjust opacity to show change (0.7 -> 0.1 and 0.7 -> 0.99)
        new_sum_text = MathTex(r"|0.1|^2 + |0.99|^2 \approx 1", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(new_sum_text, 'B3', 'B4')
        
        self.play(
            quarky_left.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            quarky_right.animate.set_opacity(0.99),
            FadeOut(sum_formula),
            FadeIn(new_sum_text)
        )
        self.wait(3)

        # Final cleanup
        self.play(
            *[FadeOut(m) for m in [formula, alpha_rect, beta_rect, room_left, room_right, label_left, label_right, quarky_left, quarky_right, new_sum_text]]
        )
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class Section3Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "Superposition & Quantum States",
            [
                "Quantum particles exist in",
                "multiple states simultaneously.",
                "This 'superposition' only",
                "collapses upon observation."
            ]
        )

        # 2. Visual Elements: Two states and a superposition state
        state_0 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        label_0 = MathTex("|0\\rangle", font_size=30).next_to(state_0, DOWN)
        state_0_group = VGroup(state_0, label_0)

        state_1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5)
        label_1 = MathTex("|1\\rangle", font_size=30).next_to(state_1, DOWN)
        state_1_group = VGroup(state_1, label_1)

        # Superposition represented by a shifting/glowing circle
        sup_state = Circle(radius=0.6, color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        sup_label = MathTex("\\frac{|0\\rangle + |1\\rangle}{\\sqrt{2}}", font_size=24).next_to(sup_state, DOWN)
        sup_group = VGroup(sup_state, sup_label)

        # 3. Placement using 6x6 Grid (Focusing on Columns 2-5 for visibility)
        self.place_at_grid(state_0_group, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(state_1_group, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(sup_group, "D4", scale_factor=1.0)

        # 4. Animations
        self.play(Write(self.title), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture, shift=RIGHT), run_time=2)
        
        self.play(Create(state_0_group), Create(state_1_group))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Draw lines to superposition
        line1 = Line(state_0_group.get_bottom(), sup_group.get_top(), color=GRAY, stroke_width=2)
        line2 = Line(state_1_group.get_bottom(), sup_group.get_top(), color=GRAY, stroke_width=2)
        
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))
        self.play(FadeIn(sup_group, scale=0.5))
        
        # Animation showing "flickering" between states to simulate superposition
        self.play(
            sup_state.animate.set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.6),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            sup_state.animate.set_fill(RED, opacity=0.6),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=0.5
        )

        self.wait(2)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        
        # Title
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=24, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        
        # Grid System for Animation Area (Right side)
        # Rows A-F, Cols 1-6
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]

        # Center the grid on the right side of the screen
        # Screen is roughly 14 units wide (-7 to 7). Lecture takes roughly 5 units.
        # Grid x starts from 1.0 to 6.0
        for i, row_label in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col_label in enumerate(cols):
                x_val = 1.5 + j * 1.0
                y_val = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row_label}{col_label}"] = np.array([x_val, y_val, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        """Helper to place mobjects on the defined 6x6 grid."""
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        if grid_pos in self.grid:
            mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        else:
            # Fallback to origin if key missing
            mobject.move_to(RIGHT * 3)
